headline: Nvidia gave the AI trade a 2028 number instead of a quarter, and Warsh gets the Jackson Hole podium on Friday.
stance: NVDA +7.2% (~6:09am ET). The beat did almost nothing after the close; the first year-ahead guide the company has ever given did all of it, and it lands on the one input every AI model has to assume.

news.head: Nvidia guided fiscal 2028 to about 70% revenue growth
news.body: Consensus sat near 44%. October quarter guided to $108bn of revenue; gross margin troughs at 71-72% in the January quarter on memory cost.

news.head: Core PCE ran 3.3% year over year in July
news.body: Core 0.2% on the month, headline 3.7%, both a tenth above consensus. Income rose 0.4% against spending up 0.2%.

news.head: The 5-year went to real money, not to dealers
news.body: $70bn cleared at 4.393%. Indirect bidders took 61.5% and dealers 10.0%, a lighter takedown than Tuesday brought at the front end.

news.head: Jackson Hole opens today
news.body: Theme is financial innovation and payments. Warsh's first symposium address as chair is Friday 10am ET, 19 days before the September decision.

implications: A 2028 commitment, not a quarter, is what the complex needed. It also moves the argument from whether the orders exist to whether memory and power get built fast enough to fill them.
Rate vol is being sold into the two events that can still reprice September. Cheap convexity and a calm week are not the same thing.

watch.head: Jobless claims, 8:30am ET
watch.body: Consensus 206k, continuing claims 1,799k. July payrolls printed negative, so this is the series September actually turns on now.

watch.head: $44bn 7-year note, 1pm ET
watch.body: Last coupon of the week and the one that asks for real duration. Dealers were left 10.0% yesterday; well above that says the bid stopped at five years.

watch.head: Whether the gap broadens or just concentrates
watch.body: 50.5% of the Nasdaq 100 closed above its 50-day line yesterday, from 58% on Friday. A gap in the largest weight hides that, it does not fix it.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Two straight sessions of sold rate vol, through a core print a tenth hot and $139bn of coupons. The market prices Friday's keynote as a non-event before hearing a word of it.
September is no longer being traded off inflation. Core at 3.3% alongside negative July payrolls is the split Warsh inherits, and the front end told you which half it weights.
sections.positioning: Standing background: spec net long 2-year Treasury at the 100th %ile of three years, four weeks running. Sold vol on top of a maxed-out long is the fragile part.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Options priced a 5.4% move and got one, in the wrong direction first: down as much as 3% on the print, then higher once the fiscal 2028 line came out on the call.
The index has gone nowhere for a week while its average member slipped underneath it. Today's gap arrives into thinner participation than the flat tape suggested.
sections.positioning: Spec net short Nasdaq 100 at the 3rd %ile of three years, three weeks running - the wrong side of a 7% move in the index's largest weight.

single_name.note: TTM Technologies - new to the screen today, printed circuit boards into the AI hardware chain, insider buy filed Aug 25, above its 200-day. One day to cover, so no short fuel.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Investment-grade spreads have not moved in a week and high yield's premium over them is where it was a week ago, through an oil break and the biggest print of the quarter.
The first widening in overnight funding in a week showed up Tuesday, before any of this week's supply has settled. Small, but month end is the direction that matters.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer investment-grade inventory sits mid-range at the 53rd %ile of three years. The balance sheet is available if next week's calendar asks for it.

single_name.note: Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance - three insider rules fired, six sessions on the screen, above its 200-day. A niche CRE lender is a spread read, not a rate one.

ideas.line: 4 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
